SOLARY CUNNING CLASS - WEDS 30TH SEPT

Happy Monday, folks. In but two short days – on Wednesday 30th September – I will be delivering my brand new class, Solary Cunning, exploring the working-books of early modern British cunning-folk and analysing their conjurations, charms, and operations for working with the Sun. 

From timing to materia, golden fairy-flowers to images of yourself in gold (and what to use instead when gold is too costly…!), and from identifying thieves through dream to stopping gossip – not to mention “conjuring the sun” itself by streamlined resort to older medieval arcana – this class will deliver a host of traditional practices and approaches to working with the diurnal luminary of empowerment and thwarting malfeasance. 

Putting this class together has already enriched my perspectives and understandings on both planetary magic and cunning-craft, and as such I can happily advise this class to anyone interested in the intersections of astrological magic and folk sorcery, as well as those looking to dive deeper into techniques and workings collected in the personal spellbooks of pre-modern service magicians. 

You can read more about what we’ll be getting into and sign up to join us from the usual 🔗🌳 hub up top. The class will of course also be recorded, and sent out to all ticket holders a few days after the live session. 

I hope you can join me for this one!

We’ve officially entered Libra season which is a time traditionally associated with balance, justice, relationships, and harmony. But the Sun’s opposition to Neptune in Aries is raising questions about what we’re being told, what we believe, and how difficult it can be to distinguish truth from illusion.

At the same time, the Sun forms trines to Uranus and Pluto, two planets associated with profound change, disruption, and the transformation of existing structures. Collectively, this astrology brings our attention to the systems we live under, our relationship to authority, and the changes taking place around us.
Venus in Scorpio squares Pluto in Aquarius, while Mars in Cancer opposes Pluto. Both aspects bring questions of power, control, security, and survival to the surface. 

On a personal level, we might notice ourselves becoming more protective of our energy, questioning certain relationships, or feeling less willing to tolerate situations that we’ve outgrown.

With the Moon in Aquarius opposing Jupiter in Leo, even our emotional reactions can feel amplified. It’s easy to become overwhelmed when there’s so much happening in the world and so much information competing for our attention.

Libra season is a reminder for us that balance isn’t the absence of conflict but it requires us to confront what’s uncomfortable, recognize injustice, and decide where we stand without sacrificing our peace in the process.

WITCH TIP: Protect your peace without disconnecting from the world. Be mindful of how much information you’re consuming, pay attention to where you’re directing your energy, and remember that you don’t have to respond to every crisis or conflict immediately.
Anyway, happy fall! May your protection candles stay lit, your discernment remain sharp, and your Halloween decorations bring you some much-needed joy.

Remembering Patricia Crowther
14 October 1927 - 24 September 2025.  Patricia Crowther was a huge supporter of the museum during her lifetime. This past weekend I travelled up to Sheffield to stay with her partner, Ian Lilleyman and to pay my respects. Just over 10 years ago, I travelled up to interview Patricia on a number of occasions, to record her experiences within the craft. Her stories were both funny and deeply moving. Her recollections of time spent with Gerald Gardner for instance, were priceless and gave much insight into the man and how he navigated the world. I am deeply honoured by the fact that Ian and Patricia decided to donate a number of significant items to the museum, some of which were collected this weekend. The first we can reveal here, is Arnold Crowther’s painting of a Moon Goddess, which could often be seen in photographs of Patricia and Gerald, hanging on the wall and was also used as the cover of the Justine Glass book, seen here. I would very much like to thank Ian for not only his hospitality, but also for entrusting us with these timeless and important items. We will be posting more of the pieces in the coming weeks up to Samhain. Simon #patriciacrowther #craftelders #geraldgardner

We at the museum would like to announce that after long consideration, we are changing our name to better reflect the museum and its collections. The museum will now be known as The Edinburgh Museum of Magic & Witchcraft.

The reason for the name change is for two reasons. One, many companies that provide services for business have regulations against “fortune-telling” and the beginning of this year our previous terminal software company cancelled our account with them because their AI-generated service picked up on the word Fortune-telling in the name of the museum. We don’t really want to see this happening again with the terminal software we are currently using now and the only way to combat this is to change the name of the museum.

Secondly, the team at the museum collectively came together and felt that although the term “fortune-telling” is acceptable in academia, its negative connotations does not reflect the items in the museum associated with divination and similar spiritual practices. There seems to be a bit of a witch hunt resurfacing regarding divination practices provided as a service, and governmental officials and companies seem to be following suit in this. I have seen esoteric shops being targeted in countries where old laws against “fortune-telling” and we want to stand in solidarity with other business that provide divination services and bring an awareness that these are a spiritual practice NOT Fortune-telling, and have been provided as a service to the community for hundreds of years. 

We have also updated our logo and now have tote bags you can purchase in our gift shop. Soon will be available to purchase on our website 😊

In just over a week, I’ll be presenting on digital libraries and the occult at moon.cultus. The webinar is entitled, “Scrying the Screen: Invoking Magic & Power Through Digital Libraries.”

Ever grateful to Melissa Madara for facilitating, and for this amazing art with ASCII + Photoshop.

I’ll place a link to the webinar in my bio & story.

The description reads:

Moon Cult is excited to welcome Danny Scopelliti, MLIS, for a look at digital libraries, archives, and resources for esoteric knowledge and occult research

The digital screen is a potent magical medium. It allows one to gaze into cyber-realms containing artifacts of magic and the occult. By scrying these materials, the practitioner, researcher, and layperson alike may partake in unique and transformative experience. As with any form of magic, a kind of ‘techne,’ or craft, is required: skills and approaches to aid and enact the full power of the medium.

As such, Scrying the Screen will guide attendees through the realm of digital library collections. This exploration aims to explore how libraries can serve as doorways for exploration centered on the visual & textual cultures of the occult sphere. 

As a feature of the digital humanities, these collections usher us towards new vistas of expression, appreciation, and practice. Skills for navigating and utilizing these tools are vital components in the journey. In turn, this event will guide attendees through suggested approaches for exploration. 

The presentation will draw on established library collections in a broad-yet-substantive survey of resources.

Featured materials will include alchemical manuscripts of a fantastical sort, ephemera from Thee Temple ov Psychick Youth, a close-up examination of a Fin de siècle magical calendar, a 1909 profile on the synesthesia of Pamela Colman Smith, and artistic considerations of an intermedia ‘grimoire’ from the French Lettrist movement.

May curiosity be your guide!

— Looking forward to seeing you there

💔VENUS RETROGRADE 💔

Venus retrograde begins today, October 3, and continues through November 13 in Scorpio and Libra. 🥀 The planet of love, beauty, pleasure, and money is taking us back through some complicated territory this spooky season.

Old lovers might resurface, along with the desires we thought we’d buried or released. An attraction can still have a hold on us even when we remember exactly why the relationship has ended. Give yourself time to remember the whole story before deciding whether you want to go there again. 🙃

In Scorpio, this retrograde can bring attention to the ways intimacy can become tangled with jealousy, secrecy, and control. We may have to admit how much we’ve tolerated because we wanted something to work, or finally speak about a desire we’ve been ashamed to acknowledge. There is room here to understand ourselves more honestly, even when what we discover is uncomfortable.

When Venus returns to Libra on October 25, those realizations can open conversations about fairness and whether our relationships allow both people to feel loved and respected. Pay attention to your relationship with money, too, especially if spending has become a way to soothe disappointment. Give yourself room to change your mind before making promises you’ll have to live with long after the urgency passes.

For a deeper look at this transit, join us over on Patreon.com/thehoodwitch for my extended Venus retrograde guide. 🕯️

Would you rather visit your ancestors in the past or meet your descendants in the future? 

October and November are months of ancestral veneration. We tend our altars, prepare offerings, and spend time honoring our dead. This year, Venus retrograde in Scorpio brings questions of love and inheritance into that practice. Some of the beliefs we’re reconsidering have been in our families longer than anyone can remember.

With Mercury also in Scorpio, I’m interested in what we could learn if we could hear the stories firsthand. Family history changes depending on who is telling it. There are things people take to the grave that everyone else spends a lifetime trying to understand.

If you could sit down with an ancestor, what would you actually ask? Would you want to know how they practiced their magic? Who taught them? Would you tell them what happened to their children or homes? 

I wonder what they would make of us. Would they recognize something they had prayed for, or have some serious questions about what the hell we’re doing. 

Meeting our descendants would put us on the other side of that conversation. We would be answering questions about our beliefs, our choices, and things we never imagined anyone would remember.

That feels like a question worth sitting with this ancestor season. Would you go back, or would you go forward? 🤔🤔

Have you already been feeling the energy shift?

What a lot of people call “spooky season” has traditionally been a time of deep ancestral reverence across many cultures. The veil feels thinner, the days get darker, and our attention naturally turns toward the dead, the unseen, and the people who came before us.

Today I felt compelled to buy cinnamon buns for my altar and burn cinnamon incense throughout my home. My ancestors are very specific about what they like, and they have always had a sweet tooth.

Cinnamon has long been used in magical practice for protection, prosperity, warmth, purification, attraction, and spiritual power. Its heat makes it especially useful for waking up stagnant energy, strengthening intention, and bringing life back into a space. I love working with it around the home when the seasons begin to change.

I also washed down my front door today. Sundays are for slowness, cooking, cleansing, tending the altar, and getting the house back in order.

I’m hosting a very chill circle tonight for my paid Patreon members, but I wanted to leave you with a little Sunday witch tip too:

Trust your instincts when it comes to spirit communication right now.

Pay attention to the foods you suddenly feel like putting on the altar. The song that keeps playing in your head. The name you keep hearing. The photograph you suddenly want to pull out. The dream that stays with you all morning. The urge to light a candle for someone you haven’t thought about in years.

Your loved ones may have very specific ways of getting your attention.

You don’t always need complicated ritual, often times our ancestor work is a cup of Black coffee, a favorite dessert, fresh water, a clean home, a white candle, and taking a few quiet minutes to slow down and just listen.

We at the museum would like to announce that after long consideration, we are changing our name to better reflect the museum and its collections. The museum will now be known as The Edinburgh Museum of Magic & Witchcraft.

The reason for the name change is for two reasons. One, many companies that provide services for business have regulations against “fortune-telling” and the beginning of this year our previous terminal software company cancelled our account with them because their AI-generated service picked up on the word Fortune-telling in the name of the museum. We don’t really want to see this happening again with the terminal software we are currently using now and the only way to combat this is to change the name of the museum.

Secondly, the team at the museum collectively came together and felt that although the term “fortune-telling” is acceptable in academia, its negative connotations does not reflect the items in the museum associated with divination and similar spiritual practices. There seems to be a bit of a witch hunt resurfacing regarding divination practices provided as a service, and governmental officials and companies seem to be following suit in this. I have seen esoteric shops being targeted in countries where old laws against “fortune-telling” and we want to stand in solidarity with other business that provide divination services and bring an awareness that these are a spiritual practice NOT Fortune-telling, and have been provided as a service to the community for hundreds of years. 

We have also updated our logo and now have tote bags you can purchase in our gift shop. Soon will be available to purchase on our website 😊

hermeticism.caption: Maymon, Demon King of the South. // According to the Grimoire of St. Cyprian, Maymon is one of the Four Demon Kings, and is attributed to the South. He is associated with a black bird, crowned and standing upon a branch, similar to the illustration found in Faust’s Magia Naturalis et Innaturalis. In Clavis Inferni, Maymon is placed in opposition to the Archangel Gabriel. He is also associated with sovereignty over other spirits, including Asmodeus, who is described as acting under his power. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Egyn, Demon King of the North. // According to the Grimoire of St. Cyprian, Egyn is one of the Four Demon Kings, and is attributed to the North. He is associated with a blue, crowned bear, representing the element of Earth. In Clavis Inferni, Egyn is placed in opposition to the Archangel Uriel. He is associated with knowledge of the natural world, hidden things, and the revelation of secrets. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Fleur-de-lis ankh. // I worked on this piece a few years ago when I first moved to New Orleans. Originally associated with the French monarchy, the fleur-de-lis arrived in Louisiana during the French colonial period and eventually became one of the city’s most recognizable emblems. The ankh symbolizes everlasting life, while the fleur-de-lis evokes New Orleans’ French heritage. The earliest versions of the fleur-de-lis were represented as scarab beetles, which the Egyptians regarded as sacred symbols of rebirth, renewal, and spiritual enlightenment. The two symbols combined celebrate New Orleans as a crossroads of history and spirituality. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

The Thoth deck. // I recently had the chance to see Lady Frieda Harris’s original paintings at the Morgan Library. Developed in collaboration with Aleister Crowley for the Thoth Tarot, Harris’s study of Rudolf Steiner’s Anthroposophy and projective synthetic geometry influenced the development of the Thoth deck, shaping its distinctive use of form, movement, and color. Seeing the paintings in person and on a large scale was a striking experience. It gave me a renewed appreciation for one of the most influential works of the modern Western esoteric tradition.

Anu, Lord of the Constellations. // Known as the Sky Father, King of the Gods, Lord of the Constellations, Anu is the divine personification of the sky, supreme God and father of all the deities in the Mesopotamian religion. He was believed to be the supreme source of all authority, for the other gods and for all mortal rulers, and he is described in one text as the one “who contains the entire universe”. He is identified with the north ecliptic pole centered in the constellation Draco. His symbol is the Dingir, a star shaped ideogram that represents the heavens. The original association of divinity is thus with the “bright” or “shining” stars in the sky. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Baphomet. // “They have built the high places of Topheth, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire, which I did not command, and it did not come into My mind.” —Jer. 7:31 // Winter Solstice, the shortest day of the year, was linked with Capricornus in the Zodiac. Eliphas Levi studied thus intently because of its connection with ceremonial magic, identifying it with Baphomet, the ass-headed idol of the Templar Knights. Still, it was greatly misunderstood. He succeeded in identifying the goat with Pan, portrayed as Pan Pangenitor, the All-Begetter. It is the male creative force, the goat leaping with lust upon the summit of the earth. It is also refers to all gods containing these correspondences, such as Sheitan or Satan. Essential to the symbolism is the surroundings, the barren places, especially high places, mountaintops. The Old Testament is full of stories of the temptation of kings who worshiped in “high places”, desolate summits uncontaminated by the deeds of men. // Sterling silver, link in profile.

Heart, skin, and flesh. // The keys to the construction of the Enochian Lamen are in the condensation of the 12x7 table containing the letters of the names of the seven planetary Heptarchic Kings and their Princes. From the outside in, the Lamen is divided into three sections: the flesh, heart, and skin. The flesh is added to the perimeter of the Lamen, then the heart to the corners of the inner square. The skin is added to the corners of the diamond square, and the remaining letters of the 12x7 table are woven in between. As the Table of Practice conciliates Heaven and earth, so does the Lamen placed over the heart conciliate the magician to the Holy Table. // Gold, link in profile.

Xeper signet ring. // I worked on this ring a few years ago. This signet ring features the hieroglyphs of Xeper: the scarab god of transformation and remanifestation, the mouth, the spoken word that creates and the scroll, the written word that preserves. I’ve always found something magical in the process of crafting and making things by hand. The artificer transforms thought into form. Taking an idea and slowly bringing it into existence mirrors the process of creating experiences. In creating something, we also create opportunities to change and become. // Sterling silver, link in profile.
